name: paddle-mcp
description: Paddle (marketplaces): me, list_products, get_product, create_product, update_price, list_sales, lis

platform_mcp_paddle_api_key.title: PLATFORM_MCP_PADDLE_API_KEY
platform_mcp_paddle_api_key.description: Paddle API key (Paddle > Developer tools > Authentication; live keys look like pdl_live_apikey_...) sent as Authorization: Bearer. Give it product.read, product.write, price.write, transaction.read, adjustment.read and adjustment.write permissions for the full tool set. Sandbox keys (pdl_sdbx_apikey_...) need base https://sandbox-api.paddle.com, which this server does not switch to.

platform_mcp_paddle_tax_category.title: PLATFORM_MCP_PADDLE_TAX_CATEGORY
platform_mcp_paddle_tax_category.description: Tax category for create_product (POST /products requires it): standard, digital-goods, ebooks, implementation-services, professional-services, saas, software-programming-services, training-services or website-hosting. Only create_product needs it.

platform_mcp_paddle_env.title: PLATFORM_MCP_PADDLE_ENV
platform_mcp_paddle_env.description: Vendor environment (default production): sandbox = https://sandbox-api.paddle.com. Credentials are the environment's own; see adapter.environments in the catalog entry.

platform_mcp_paddle_base_url.title: PLATFORM_MCP_PADDLE_BASE_URL
platform_mcp_paddle_base_url.description: Optional https base URL override (a mock or a private gateway); replaces the selected environment's base_url. Never echoed in errors.

tools.name: me
tools.description: GET /event-types (no specific permission listed) answers {data[{name, description, group, available_versions}], meta{request_id}}; it verifies the API key and the environment. Paddle has no account/me endpoint.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: GET /products?include=prices&per_page (1-200, default 50)&status (active|archived; Paddle defaults to active). `price`/`currency` come from the product's first included price (unit_price.amount is a STRING in the currency's lowest denomination, e.g. "1000" = 10.00 USD; other prices stay in raw.prices). Paging is by cursor (`after` from meta.pagination.next), which page/limit cannot carry: `page` is ignored and only the first page is returned; `total` is not mapped (estimated_total may be -1).

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: GET /products/{product_id}?include=prices returns data{id, name, description, tax_category, type, image_url, custom_data, status, created_at, updated_at, prices[]}; `price`/`currency` are the first price's unit_price (amount as a string in the lowest denomination).

tools.name: create_product
tools.description: POST /products {name (required, 1-200 chars), description, tax_category (required by Paddle, taken from the tax_category setting; a 400 upstream_error means it is unset)}. Paddle products carry no price: `price`/`currency` are NOT sent — call update_price afterwards to create the price entity. The product is created active; `url` is not accepted (image_url is not a product page).

tools.name: update_price
tools.description: Paddle prices are separate entities, so this CREATES a new active price for the product with POST /prices {description (required internal note, fixed), product_id, unit_price{amount, currency_code}}; existing prices stay active until archived (PATCH /prices/{price_id} status=archived, not mapped). `price` is sent as the documented STRING in the currency's lowest denomination — pass an integer such as 1000 for 10.00 USD (a decimal is rejected). `currency` is required by Paddle. The result's `id` is the product id; the new price id is raw.id (pri_...).

tools.name: list_sales
tools.description: GET /transactions?include=customer&per_page (max 30)&created_at[GTE]=since (RFC 3339), newest first (default order id[DESC]). `amount` is details.totals.total, a STRING in the lowest denomination after discount and tax; `product_id`/`product_name` come from the first line item's price. There is no product filter, so `product_id` is not sent. Cursor paging (`after`) cannot be carried by page/limit: `page` is ignored and only the first page is returned. `refunded` is not a transaction field (see list_refunds).

tools.name: list_refunds
tools.description: GET /adjustments?action=refund&per_page (default 10, max 50), newest first. `amount` is totals.total (string, lowest denomination); `status` is pending_approval, approved, rejected or reversed. The endpoint has no date filter, so `since` is not sent; chargebacks are action=chargeback (not listed here). Cursor paging: `page` is ignored, first page only.

tools.name: refund
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE: POST /adjustments {action: refund, transaction_id: sale_id (txn_...), reason, type: full} requests a FULL refund of the transaction. `amount` is NOT sent and does not limit the refund: a partial adjustment needs items[{item_id, type, amount}] per transaction item, which this input cannot express — call the API directly for partial refunds. `reason` is required by Paddle (a missing reason is a 400 upstream_error). On live accounts the adjustment is created as pending_approval and reviewed by Paddle; sandbox approves automatically.
